examples.text: The risk is a two-story, Masonry Non-Combustible (MNC) (ISO-4) building with an unfinished basement. Tenants include Sparrow Pizza Restaurant and Westfield Bank on the ground floor and law offices on the upper floor. The building is fully occupied. The risk was built in 1936 with the current owner acquiring it in 2019. The building measures 31,756 square feet, excluding the unfinished basement and a parking area for the tenants of 6,750 sq. ft. There have been no reported damages or losses. The exterior walls are made of concrete block with a brick veneer. The roof is metal beam with metal/concrete decking and a rubber membrane covering. The interior walls are sheetrock. The ceilings are acoustic panels in the bank, the offices on the second floor, and some areas of the restaurant. Some ceilings are sheetrock. The floors are tiled and cement in the restaurant, while the bank and the offices on the second floor have carpet over metal/concrete. The utilities are safely arranged and comply with local codes. Electric is BX cable with circuit breaker protection. The plumbing is copper, iron, and PVC. Heating and air conditioning are provided by a gas/oil-fueled HVAC system. The restaurant features a full commercial kitchen with a currently inspected hood/exhaust, AES, and K-type fire extinguisher. Interior walking surfaces are smooth, level, and free of trip/fall hazards. The lighting is good throughout. Stairs are stable with secure handrails. The sidewalks are smooth and level. Signs are well-secured. The building is fully sprinkler-protected and the required fire extinguishers have been inspected and noted in their prescribed locations. The fire alarm is monitored by Encore. The building is served by the paid West Hartford Fire Department, located at 95 Raymond Rd, West Hartford, CT 06107, approximately 0.6 miles away. The city provides an adequate water supply, with the nearest fire hydrant located 30 feet from the property. The restaurant, bank, and offices each have a centrally monitored burglar alarm and video cameras, though the name of the monitoring company for the burglar alarms was not provided. The surrounding area includes both residential and mercantile properties. Housekeeping and maintenance are very good. The overall structural condition of the building is good.

The risk is a two-story, joisted masonry (ISO-2) multiple-tenant, mixed-use building with an unfinished basement. The ground floor is occupied by Bricco Restaurant and NY Grill and Deli, while the upper floors feature offices for The Mission Escape, Sara Quish-Social Worker, and the Book Club. The building is 100% occupied. The risk was constructed in 1953 and has been owned by the insured for two years. The building measures 11,200 SF excluding the unfinished basement and a tenant parking area of 7,500 square feet. There have been no reported damages or losses. The exterior consists of concrete block with brick veneer. The roof is metal joists with wood decking covered by a rubber membrane. The interior walls are sheetrock. The ceilings are acoustic panels in both the restaurants and the offices. The floors are a mix of tile and carpet over wood. The utilities are safely arranged and comply with local codes. The electric is BX cable with circuit breaker protection. The plumbing is copper and PVC. Heating and air conditioning come from a gas/oil-fueled HVAC system. Both restaurants have a full commercial kitchen with hood/exhaust, AES, and K-type fire extinguisher. Neither restaurant has a currently inspected hood/exhaust or AES. The interior walking surfaces are smooth, even, and free of trip/fall hazards. The lighting is good throughout. Stairs are stable with secure handrails. The sidewalks are smooth and level. Signs are securely attached. The building does not have sprinkler protection, however, currently inspected fire extinguishers were noted where prescribed. The area is protected by the paid West Hartford Fire Department, located at 95 Raymond Rd, West Hartford, CT 06107, approximately 0.5 miles away. The city of West Hartford provides an adequate water supply with the nearest fire hydrant being 105' from the risk. Each tenant has a centrally monitored burglar alarm and video cameras. The surrounding area is a mix of residential and mercantile properties. Housekeeping and maintenance are good. The overall structural condition of the building is good.

NOTE: Visit was requested to get into an apartment and the restaurant, as these areas were not accessible during the previous visit. I was able to accomplish these tasks. The insured owns a mixed use property at this location in the Chinatown area of Philadelphia. The property has an adult day care on the 1021 side and a cafe on the 1023 side of the building. There are also 10 apartments on the upper floors of the building. The entire building is occupied at this time, no vacant space. The insured purchased the property in 2011 and did a gut renovation in 2012. The building is three stories, joisted masonry with a full unfinished basement. The walls are solid masonry that bear the load of the structure. The floors are wood on wood joists. The roof is also wood on wood joists with a rubber covering. The roof was replaced in 2012. The building was built in 1930 and has a total square footage of 9450 SF for the upper and 3150 for the basement. There are gas fired hot air heating and central air units throughout the property. The electrical systems are breakers, romex and bx wiring, all copper. Domestic water is circulated in copper and drained in PVC. All of the utilities were replaced in 2012. Housekeeping was good. The restaurant has a commercial cooking exposure. They have proper service on the fire suppression system. The quarterly hood cleaning was done in November 2024 and is due in February 2025. The service company was busy and will be doing the visit on 2/25/2025, per the tenant. They have a K rated fire ext with annual service in place. There is a partial sprinkler system that was installed in part of the building. The system was installed in the hallway and first floor through the 1021 side of the building. The city required this system due to the adult day care that moved into the building. The system has not been serviced in the last year, see rec. In addition, the caps are missing off the fire department connection in front of the building, see rec. They have ABC fire ext throughout the building with annual service. There are hard wired smoke detectors and manual pull fire alarms in place. The Philadelphia Fire Department is paid and within a block of the site. They have hydrants on the street and the PPC is a 1. They have proper egress, including emergency lights and illuminated exit signs. The walks are properly maintained. Interior and exterior steps have rails and are properly maintained. They have good lighting on site.

The insured leases this warehouse space to the City of Greenville for the purpose of operating the Parks and Recreation Department. The building has split use with offices, kitchen, equipment storage, and a workshop area. The building is an 8,160 square foot, single-story, ISO Construction Class-4 commercial warehouse structure built in 1940. The exterior walls are brick veneer with wood framing. The interior walls are brick veneer and concrete. The foundation appears to be poured concrete. The roof is wood and concrete decking, with a metal roof supported with steel purlins. Building heat is provided by HVAC using electric. The electrical system predominantly consists of BX cable with circuit breaker protection. Plumbing consists primarily of galvanized, PVC, and PEX piping. All utilities were updated in 2024. The building is in good overall condition with adequate maintenance practices in place. Housekeeping was noted to be good. Exits are clearly marked and lighted. Egress to all exits is good with a place of safety beyond the exits. Interior lighting is adequate. Emergency lighting is in place. Interior floor surfaces are smooth and level with no slip / trip and fall hazards noted. Exterior lighting was noted to be adequate. Exterior driveways, parking areas, sidewalks and walkway surface exposures are controlled with no slip / trip and fall hazards noted. There were no weather-related hazards noted. The building is protected by ID card entry system and doors are always locked. The City of Greenville installed cameras with coverage in the entire interior and exterior of the building, including the property perimeter. There is also a 12'ft fence surrounding exterior storage area that is ID card entry system equipped as well. The building is not sprinkler system protected; however it is central fire protected. There is a pull station and fire extinguisher, properly mounted and tagged on premises. Smoke detectors are hard-wired to the electric service with battery backup and a local alarm, and it is connected to the central station. Public fire protection is provided by the City of Greenville Fire Department Station 2, a Class 1, full-time, paid fire department. It is located 1.5 miles away from the insured location. Fire department / EMS response time would be approximately 7 minutes. There is a history of flooding in the area surrounding the property. The building and property are located in FEMA flood Zone AE (An area at high risk of flooding. It indicates a 1% annual chance of experiencing a flood event, commonly referred to as the 100-year floodplain. In these areas, floodwaters are more likely to reach certain elevations during severe weather events.). The property is located near a low-lying area and there is exposure to run-off or flash flooding. There is a river, Reedy River, located approximately 100'ft from the property. The building is located in a commercial business park area located directly in a large public park, Unity Park. The warehouses located in this commercial area have been converted into other businesses such as restaurants, specialty shops, and a farmers' market. The location provides easy access to Greenville's busy downtown area and the Interstate highway system. The business park is a busy, urban commercial area of Greenville County. There are no high hazard businesses or high hazard business operations in the neighborhood or area. There are no vacant or abandoned buildings noticed in the neighborhood or area. There were no signs of vandalism, or graffiti noted anywhere in the neighborhood and business park area.

The insured located at 3100 Lakeland Dr, Flowood, MS operates as the Jackson Preparatory School, a private preparatory school which includes approximately 84 acres of surrounding property. The building Jackson prep. lower school includes a two-story section which was built in 2024 and is of ISO IV construction. The total square footage is approximately 25.540 SF. The two-story section includes the reception area and offices includes a Library. The roof, electrical, plumbing and HVAC were from construction in 2024 and with no deficiencies or code violations observed or reported. No roof or plumbing leaks were noted. All wiring appears to be in good condition and is enclosed in conduit and protected by circuit breakers. Fire doors or firewalls were observed. The floors observed were all clean, swept and vacuumed at least daily. The layout of the premises is conducive to the instruction and activities conducted. The classroom areas appear to be adequate to accommodate the size of the classes and all instructional materials and equipment. There is adequate spacing between student desks. The bookshelves and cabinets are solidly constructed and secured from tip over. There are separate boys' and girls' restrooms in each classroom. Instructional areas and hallways appear to have good housekeeping and are free of debris and clutter. The floors and floor coverings are all in good condition with mats and other coverings securely anchored. The floors observed were all clean, swept and vacuumed at least daily. All areas are well ventilated and well lit. Egress is adequate with unobstructed doors opening outward with panic hardware and lighted exit signs above the exit doors. Emergency lighting was observed in the building. There are stairways adjoining the one-story section to the two-story section of the building. Sidewalks and parking areas are free of cracks, potholes and other trip/fall hazards. Student drop-off/pick-up points are safely removed from passing traffic and with staff monitors provided to assist. 100 % of the 25,540 SF building is protected with a wet sprinkler system. The areas where the fire sprinkler system is located are in climate-controlled areas and the sprinkler system appears to be in good working order. The sprinkler main valve appeared to be in the open position with extra sprinkler heads and a wrench. Sprinkler system is contracted and inspected every 12 months by Southeastern automatic sprinkler company with the last inspection date 05/2024. Pull down fire alarm systems with pull stations at all exit doors were observed and are monitored by Simplex Grinnell. The fire extinguishers were of the correct type and number and strategically located and currently tagged. The smoke detectors are hard wired with battery backup and monitored by Director of School Safety. Public fire protection for this area is provided by the paid Flowood City Fire Department. The ISO class is listed at 3. The nearest noted fire station is less than one mile from this location. They are on public water supply. The nearest noted fire hydrant is around 40 feet from the building. There is a central station burglar alarm that is monitored by Grinnell monitoring company. The school campus is equipped with CCTV cameras. There are 30 surveillance cameras around the property inside and out and with security entry cards and intercom systems at each entry door to the classroom buildings. There are no uniform security guards on the premises. There are no hazardous occupancies within 100 feet of the risk. No overhanging tree limbs and/or large dead or dying trees within 100 feet and with no brush or other natural exposures, and no nearby bodies of water. The neighborhood is stable and free of evidenced vandalism and/or malicious mischief activity.

The risk is a 9-story office building. The building has 3,520 square feet on each floor, with a total floor area of 31,680 square feet for the building. Occupancy appears stable, and the owner reports a total of four floors which are currently vacant; # 3, 4, 5, and 7. Vacant units are kept locked until occupied. The insured has owned the building for 38 years. No loss history was reported. The 9-story building is masonry non-combustible ISO IV construction and built in 1907 and appears structurally sound and in good condition. The exterior walls have brick veneer, with plaster interior walls and ceilings. The floor is ceramic tile over concrete at ground level. The windows observed were free of cracks. No graffiti was observed on the facade. The roof is flat and covered with membrane, updated in 2008. The building has HVAC units installed on the roof. No leaks or damage to the roof were observed or reported. The electrical system consists of conduits and a junction box, with over-current breakers; everything appears well installed and in good condition. Maintenance is good, with no trash or debris in the common areas. Vacant units are free of debris, etc., while new updates, painting, and other minor improvements are being completed. The entry door to the building has an intercom and a keypad for entry. Exterior lighting is provided with streetlights and lamps installed throughout the property. The office building has 100% sprinklers installed. At the time of the inspection, the sprinkler company did not have the inspection date labels. However, the owner sent me the certificate from the sprinkler company, which is attached. Each unit also has a fire extinguisher labeled 2A10BC. The Jackson Fire Department, located less than a mile from the hazard and serving potable water, is providing public protection. The nearest fire hydrant is located less than 10 feet away. No other special exposures were observed in the immediate area. The neighborhood appears stable, although it is primarily composed of high-rise commercial buildings.

The insured is set up as a limited partnership company dba as SRC 198 Milltown, LLC located at 1127 Welcome Way in Burlington, NC. This location serves as the rental office and Club House for 198 Milltown Apartment Homes, 481 Perimeter Loop and 1127 Welcome Way, Burlington, NC 27215 apartment buildings. The offices hours of the leasing office are Monday-Friday 9:00am- 6:00pm, 10:00am- 5:00pm and they closed on Sunday. It is an ideal location that is steps away from Alamance Crossings Shopping Center and Greensboro Science Center. Right off 1-40 E and Bonnar Bridge Pkwy, major employers and schools such as Laboratory Corporation of America and Glen Raven are within reach. Restocking the fridge and pantry, updating your wardrobe, and meeting up with friends is all possible to do without having to go too far from our doorstep. There are many hot spots close by or easily accessible in Greensboro. The 198 Milltown Clubhouse is Frame ISO-I Masonry Construction on a cement foundation, approximately 5744 total sf. with one 1 flr. The roof is a gable roof covered with shingles. It is supported by a circuit breaker, but wiring is not observed, plumbing is not observed, heating is provided by HVAC units. There are smoke detectors, but no carbon monoxide detectors were observed. There is a standpipe, sprinklers and fire extinguishers with up-to-date inspection tags. There are illuminated exit signs and emergency lights observed. The 198 Milltown Clubhouse amenities are a 24-hour resident lounge, 24-hr. cycle lounge, on-demand fitness, salt water swimming pool, pet park playground, garages, pet spa, pool table, indoor firepit, outdoor social lounge, outdoor grilling Pavillion, complimentary Starbucks Coffee, 24-hr. health club, conference room, 24-hr Amazon Hub Package Lockers, clubhouse featuring a kitchenette, controlled access, a business center and car care center. Due to presence of residents using amenities photos are limited. The 481 Perimeter Loop Apartments are Frame ISO-I Construction on a cement foundation, approximately 30672 total sf. with each 3 flrs. measuring approximately 10224sf. The roof is a gable roof covered with shingles. The exterior walls consist of wood and stone. It consists of 24 units with no vacancies. It is supported by a circuit breaker, but wiring or plumbing is not observed. Heating is provided by HVAC units for each apartment. There are smoke detectors, but no carbon monoxide detectors were observed. There is a standpipe, sprinklers and fire extinguishers with up-to-date inspection tags. There are illuminated exit signs and emergency lights in the breezeway area. The 481 Perimeter Loop Apartment building consists of one, two- or three-bedroom apartments. The apartments come with a washer and dryer, walk-in closets, spacious bedrooms, also feature private patio or balcony and granite countertops. The 1127 Welcome Way Apartments are Frame-ISO-I Construction on a cement foundation, approximately 29082 total sf. with each 3 flrs. measuring approximately 9694sf. The roof is a gable roof covered with shingles. The exterior walls consist of wood and stone. It consists of 24 units with 4 vacancies. It is supported by a circuit breaker, but wiring or plumbing is not observed. Heating is provided by HVAC units for each apartment. There are smoke detectors, but no carbon monoxide detectors were observed. There is a standpipe, sprinklers and fire extinguishers with up-to-date inspection tags. There are illuminated exit signs and emergency lights in the breezeway area. The 1127 Welcome Way Apartment building consists of one, two- or three-bedroom apartments. The apartments come with a washer and dryer, walk-in closets, spacious bedrooms, also feature private patio or balcony and granite countertops. Mr. Dawson the technician was very cooperative in showing inspector around the site. There are no reported losses, since construction in 2020. The maintenance/housekeeping is excellent. There is no observation of debris or trash in the interior and exterior. Public areas, such as the lawn are well manicured and there are no bushes/shrubbery near either structure. The exterior steps that lead up to the second and third floors of 481 Perimeter and 1127 Welcome Way are in excellent condition and non-combustible. The parking lot to the front of both locations is level and smooth. There is handicapped parking. The interior lights are excellent. The property is not fenced and there is no observation of a body of water in proximity. The risk is sprinkled 100% sprinkled and has a wet sprinkler system. There are fire extinguishers mounted, with up-to-date tags throughout the structures. There are emergency lights, The central fire alarm system is monitored by Burglar Alarm Protection System, Inc. There are fire hydrants strategically located throughout the site. There are no crime related incidents reported. There are no security guards, but there is a security system. There are security cameras in and around the site. The doors are secured. There is no attached or detached, below level or ground level garage for the risk. The risk is in a residential area, which is protected by the Alamance Fire Department. This fire station is 0.4 miles from the risk.

The insured entity is a newly constructed apartment complex on the western outskirts of Raleigh NC. It is located adjacent to the upscale Brier Creek shopping district and residential area. Construction began in 2024. It consists of four primary residential buildings with an additional small 1200 sq ft satellite frame structure housing a maintenance shop and a pet spa. Three of the buildings are currently complete and partially occupied, with the fourth building still under interior construction; completion of that building is expected later this year. As of the visit date, there were 224 units that were available for rent, with 81 currently being vacant. When the fourth building is completed, there will be an additional 52 units for a total of 276 units. The current vacancy is estimated at 54 percent, but this is a new complex with highly competitive rents for the area, and a 95% occupancy rate is projected for October 2025 or sooner. All parking is exterior surface lot. There are no garages or carport coverings offered. Rents range from $1,300 for the smallest one-bedroom units up to approximately $2,000 for the largest two-bedroom units. Tenants pay their own utilities, plus a quarterly pest control surcharge. Small to medium pets are allowed, with owners having to pay a monthly pet surcharge. One-bedroom units all have one bath and a balcony, comma, with two-bedroom units having two baths, with two-bedroom units have two baths and a balcony. All buildings are four-story ISO Class-1 frame structures built on slab and concrete and steel footings. Roofs are a modified hip style covered with asphalt shingles. Building #7900 contains the residents' clubhouse of 4,187 sq ft as well as the leasing office. It is L-shaped and contains 47,200 square feet of heated space in four stories, with a swimming pool adjacent to the exterior of the clubhouse area. The additional three buildings are #7920, #7931, and #7940 (7940 is still under construction). All three of these buildings are identical in size and shape, being rectangular with 50,148 square feet of space in each, and are also four stories period. The interior construction consists of frame walls with sheet rock for walls and ceilings, and vinyl plank flooring. All buildings have elevators serviced by Otis and also have metal frame stairways with concrete treads. Apartments each have their own electric hot water heaters and HVAC units. One unit was inspected in #7900 and another in #7920. Entry to all units is obtained from hallways, described as breezeways because they are unheated. There are secured entries to the breezeways. These consist of heavy perforated metal steel doors and screening. Tenants must use a code or a key fob to enter. Breezeways have concrete floors, are equipped with smoke detectors and sprinkler heads, and have fire extinguishers. Video cameras cover all hallways and stairs. This is also true of the leasing office and clubhouse. There is no monitoring of the video surveillance, but it is recorded to a hard drive and can be used to validate past events if an issue of some sort occurs and is reported. There are standpipes outdoors, adjacent to each of the buildings. All of the buildings are fully sprinklered, Additionally, there are at least three public fire hydrants on adjacent streets. The riser rooms for each building are accessed from the exterior. Due to a requirement from local fire enforcement officials, the riser rooms must have an external heating system to ensure that they do not freeze in the event there is unusually cold weather during the winter months. There are fire extinguishers at appropriate intervals in all of the breezeways and in the leasing office and clubhouse, but fire extinguishers are not provided inside the apartments themselves (note: all appliances in the apartments are electric). At this time, there are no current inspection tags because this is a new installation operating under a recently issued CO (Certificate of Occupancy), and none of the sprinklers or the extinguishers are due for the annual inspection. Raleigh NC Fire Department, a fully paid organization rated ISO Class-1, provides protection with Station 29 being 3.3 miles or 7 minutes distant. All of the public areas and the individual apartments have individual smoke alarms that are hardwired with battery backup. Each apartment, as well as the leasing office and clubhouse, has a universal alarm providing an audible signal in the event that a fire alarm is triggered anywhere in that building, in addition to having a separate visual alarm that flashes a strobe light under similar conditions. The overall construction quality and building protection measures, as well as the knowledgeable property manager Britney Womack, and highly experienced maintenance manager Sheldon Boone are all factors that support rating this as a very good risk.

The risk is a 3-story over unfinished basement, joisted masonry (ISO-2) mixed-use building, constructed in 1915, currently occupied by a restaurant, DBA NIRVANA Indian Kitchen, which serves Indian cuisine on the ground floor, and 2 residential apartments located on the second and third floors. The building is 100% occupied. The total square footage for this building is 2,532. The building's exterior walls are brick. The roof is wood joist with wood decking and rolled asphalt covering. The interior walls and ceilings are made of Sheetrock, and the floors are tile over wood. The electrical system is BX cables protected by circuit breakers. Plumbing is constructed from PVC, cast iron, and copper materials. The building uses rooftop units (RTUs) for heating and cooling. The interior walking surfaces are free of tripping hazards, with adequate lighting throughout. Stairs are sturdy, equipped with secure handrails, and well-maintained. Illuminated exit signs and emergency lighting are visibly placed. The external sidewalks are in good condition, being smooth and level. At the time of the inspection, all fire extinguishers were currently inspected. Smoke detectors are hard-wired in all common areas. A fire alarm system was noted. The Philadelphia Fire Department, located 1 mile from the building, provides emergency services, and the property has a sufficient water supply, with a fire hydrant located 40 feet from the building. The restaurant kitchen is equipped with a U.L. 300-compliant fire protection system. A K-type fire extinguisher could not be located. The exhaust system is serviced every six months, and the AES tank has a current service tag. The kitchen floors are ceramic tile over wood, with nonslip mats in place. The walls are backed with stainless steel, and the duct system vents through the exterior wall for proper exhaust. The risk has security cameras covering all exterior sides as well as general interior areas. There are no significant external exposures, as the property is located in a stable residential neighborhood. Housekeeping and maintenance practices are satisfactory, and the overall structural condition of the building is sound.

2025 The insured is the Washington Oddfellows home, and its current configuration consists of foru buildings located in a campus-like environment in Walla Walla Washington. It has been in business since 1929, providing a variety of services to the community. The complex is divided into four areas that will be addressed in four different parts of this report. Total annual revenue was $27,103,392-However that included two items which should be deducted as they did not pertain to normal operations: Gain on Sale of Apartments $8,289,400.81 (see note to U/W in Special U/W concerns), and Endowment fund donation of for loan payoff $6,128,403.75 Net Revenues from standard operations are $12,685,487.44 Note that 2023 Revenues also includedan Endowment fund donation of 2.6 million. Annual payroll is $6,928,460.16 and there are 143 employees (contract/part time/full time). It operates as a nonprofit, and it is accredited by CMS. The date of the last report is September. 2023 and there were no recommendations. Its license has not been suspended or revoked and there have been no allegations or incidents of physical or sexual abuse made. 1-Red brick bldg.-Apartments and or Offices- three stories on basement, 26,776 sf, ISO 6 construction and built in 1929. The roof is rubber (resurfaced in 2009) and HVAC is packaged RTU/1996, tested quarterly, Heat pump system-2005, quarterly, 6 ductless mini-splits systems/various years, quarterly, steam boiler for heat 2017,three 100-gallon water heaters-2017/ centrally monitored fire alarm and burglar alarm system/ Fully sprinklered, properly mounted and tagged fire extinguishers throughout, protection class is 3 and 2 miles to fire department. 2-West Care, one story,24,534 sf, ISO 6 construction, built in 1960/1992/2015, roof covered in 2017,1992 and 2015, packaged RTU/ 1999 & 2022/quarterly. Water heaters for 1960 supplied by bldg.1-1 bldgs., /2017- water heaters for 1992 and 2015 come from 1992 section/ Fully sprinklered, properly mounted and tagged fire extinguishers throughout, protection class is 3 and 2 miles to fire department. 3-TLC wing/offices/ dining/commercial kitchen-4 stories over basement, 101,492 sf, ISO 6 construction, built in 1979, roof recovered in 2011, packaged RTU 1996-2022/quarterly. Two 250 gallon and one 100-gallon water heaters-2020, monitored fire alarm and burglar alarm system/ Fully sprinklered, properly mounted and tagged fire extinguishers throughout, protection class is 3 and 2 miles to fire department. 4-Paint & Grounds Bldg.- one story on slab, ISO 2(joisted masonry construction), 2,372 sf and built in 1999.Heat is electric, not sprinklered, properly mounted and tagged fire extinguisher- protection class is 3 and 2 miles to fire department. Risk Management and Staffing Per the contact Billie Williams, there is a formal risk management program. All drugs are stored in a access-controlled medication room that is locked and staffed 24/7. The insured will arrange for medical treatment for any injured resident. There are proper first aid kits throughout the complex, and all staff have been trained. There are AEDs in several places and all staff have been trained. Evacuation and fire drills are conducted quarterly. There are handrails at all stairs, and there are fire doors in all hallways throughout, except for the Paint & Grounds Bldg. Hot water temperature is maintained at 120 degrees.

This risk is an ice cream parlor and 2 tenant occupied apartments housed in a 2 story 1930s-constructed joisted masonry building. Total area is approx. 2700sf. Insured has owned this property since 1986. There is one apartment on the 1st and one on the 2nd floor. Building is fully occupied. Please note: access to ice cream parlor was unavailable at time of inspection. Per insured there is no commercial cooking on site. No recent losses reported by the insured. Risk building appears structurally sound, in good repair and with updates, as required. The exterior load bearing walls are brick. The roof deck is over wood joisting, and per insured with rubber covering and with covering annually maintained, noting no observed or reported roof leaks or evidenced water intrusion at time of inspection. All building utilities and services appear to be properly arranged, well maintained, and in compliance with current local codes. Wiring is all on circuit breakers and appearing to code and safely arranged. Plumbing is variably copper and PVC and in satisfactory condition. Heat is supplied by individual baseboard hot water boilers. Flooring/floor covering all appears in good condition. Housekeeping observed to be uniformly good, with no observed exterior or interior trash or debris. The building is not sprinklered. There is, however, a CS fire alarm and pull stations for this risk. Portable ABC fire extinguishers in apartments. Exterior lighting is adequate. Observed A/C unit lacking metal support brackets. Sidewalk and interior walkways are smooth, even and free of trip hazards. Stairway to 2nd floor with non-slip treads and secure handrail. 2nd floor with egress directly to street level. Exit door with illuminated exit sign and emergency lights. No special external exposures were noted, with risk located in a stable, urban, lower middle-income, mixed-use area, which is protected by a paid fire department located within 1 mile, and with no obstruction to response noted. There is a good distribution of hydrants in the area, on a public water main supply grid, and with at least one hydrant within 50-feet of this building. The area is patrolled by Passaic police.

The risk, Coventry Place Apartments, located at 309 Brooke Ave, Magnolia, NJ, was constructed in 1962. It is an apartment complex consisting of eight joisted masonry (ISO-2) buildings (A-H), with a total of 156 apartment units with all apartments leased but not all yet occupied. The buildings were constructed in 1962. The total square footage of all buildings is 134,358 SF. There have been no reported losses or damage to the buildings. Each building includes a laundry room exclusively for tenant use. The laundry rooms have good housekeeping, correctly vented dryers, clean lint traps, and no standing water. The community also features an in-ground swimming pool; however, it was closed and covered at the time of the inspection. According to the property manager, the pool is expected to reopen during the warmer months, though they could not recall its total depth or size during the inspection. Numerous issues were noted with the swimming pool and recommendations were made. The exterior walls of the buildings are brick with a partial hard stucco finish. The roofs are wood joist with wood decking and rolled asphalt coverings. The interior walls and ceilings are drywall. The floors are laminate and carpet over wood. The electrical system includes BX cables with circuit breaker protection. Plumbing consists of PVC, cast iron, PEX, and copper materials. The buildings are heated by boilers, with through-wall units providing cooling. Interior walking surfaces are smooth, even, and free of trip/fall hazards. The lighting is good throughout. Stairs are sturdy, equipped with secure handrails, and well-maintained. Sidewalks and parking areas are in good condition, being smooth and level. Parking areas with lined spaces, curb protection, and adequate dusk to dawn lighting. Illuminated exit signs and emergency lighting are visibly placed. The buildings are not sprinkler protected, however, properly mounted and inspected fire extinguishers were noted where prescribed. Smoke detectors are hard-wired in all common areas. The volunteer Magnolia Fire Company, located less than a mile from the complex, provides emergency services. The property has a sufficient water supply, with multiple fire hydrants located near the buildings. Security cameras cover all exterior sides and general interior areas. There are no significant external exposures, as the property is situated in a stable residential neighborhood. This risk is a small 3-tenant mercantile building housed in a 1-story on slab 1987 constructed ISO-Class IV masonry non-combustible building. The vape store sells e-cigs and e-cig fluid, glass pipes, candles, etc., but does not sell any tobacco products or any CBD or THC type A products. The total area is approx. 4,560 sq ft. All Leases are triple net, with the exception that if the roof or parking lot are totally replaced, the building owner pays. The tenants must pay for any repairs to the roof or lot. Occupancy is stable, with operations appearing to be successful and well-managed. The location is directly across from the North Carolina State University campus, with a population of nearly 38,000 full and part time students. Foot traffic in the area is heavy, and reported crime is low. No loss history was apparent when the building was inspected, and no recent losses were reported by the contact or tenants. The risk building appears structurally sound and in overall good repair. The exterior load bearing walls are concrete block, solid full thickness brick veneer. The roof deck is described as being over metal joists, but the deck could not be seen from the inside due to the presence of solid ceiling material. No observed or reported roof leaks or evidenced water intrusion was seen at the time of inspection. The roof was replaced in 2014 and is comprised of EPDM rubber with stone ballast. No other major upgrades have been made since 2003, except for a new parking lot in 2021. All building utilities and services appear to be properly arranged, well maintained, and in compliance with current local codes. Wiring is all on circuit breakers, appears to adhere to code, and is safely arranged. Plumbing is variably copper and PVC and is in satisfactory condition. There are prep sinks in two of the spaces, with all three having private bathrooms for the employees. HVAC systems that heat and cool are on the roof, which has no interior hatch and no exterior ladder. It could not be accessed at the time of inspection. If any HVAC units fail or need repair, it is the responsibility of the tenants under the NNN lease. Flooring/floor covering all appears in good condition. Housekeeping was observed to be uniformly good, with no observed exterior or interior trash or debris. The building is not sprinklered. There is no hard wired automatic fire detection system for this risk. The vape shop and bagel shop each have a second means of egress via secure metal locked doors that access a common hallway and lead to a rear parking lot entrance. The cookie shop has no second means of egress, but customers are not allowed past the front serving counter area. The rear steps are comprised of poured concrete and are in overall acceptable condition, but one top corner has chipped off, and there are three risers with no safety railing for employees or delivery vendors using these steps. It is assumed that the lack of railing is intentional in order to more easily facilitate deliveries by ramp from small box trucks, but a recommendation is being made to add a railing. Brueggers Ste 102, and Insomnia Ste 104 had Portable Class C fire extinguishers with current inspection dates, but one of the two extinguishers at Insomnia Cookies was on the floor and not mounted in the designated space on the wall. HighLife Ste 106 did not have a portable fire extinguisher that could be found on the premises. There are no K-class fire extinguishers in the bagel shop or cookie shop, but neither of them has an open flame, and they do not do any cooking that requires a hood, Ansul system, or K-class extinguishers. The cookie shop has an electric oven and bakes thawed frozen dough that is shipped to them from an Insomnia commissary; they do not prepare ingredients on site. The bagel shop uses premade raw bagel dough provided by the Bruegger's commissary. The bagels are boiled in large kettles, which are heated by enclosed gas burners, then baked in electric ovens. The store manager stated that they are switching to electrically heated kettles, but was uncertain of the timeline for this. The boiling kettles have a vent through the roof for steam, and the bagel ovens have a hood with fan fan-powered duct. Inspection tags on the hood show that it is inspected and cleaned 4 times annually (cleaning only if required). Tenants are responsible for their own burglar alarm/central station alarms. All three tenants have burglar alarms that ring out to central monitoring companies. Exterior lighting is adequate. Risk exists with street parking on the side and front of the building, but there are raised sidewalks as well as tables mounted to the sidewalks along the front of the building, and a low 25 mph speed limit, thus reducing the likelihood of vehicular damage to storefronts. The property has 7 buildings on premises. The complex is new and construction started in late 2023. The project is nearly complete. At the time of survey the occupancy rate was 30%. This apartment complex is new construction, and the housing market in Charlotte is considered to be depressed. Approximately 15,000 new apartment units were added to the market in 2024. The increase in supply has created a higher vacancy rate. Property managers (competitors) are offering lower rates and additional concessions (move in specials - free rent for 1 to 2 months) in order to attract tenants. The neighborhood appears to be stable and no evidence of vandalism or malicious mischief was observed in the surrounding exposures. The local police department patrols the area routinely. Exterior lighting is adequate. Illuminated exit signs and emergency lighting are provided in all buildings. No deficiencies were observed.

Note to underwriter: The risk mailing address is Apex, NC but the building is located within the township of Cary, NC and is subject to all of its municipal ordinances. The risk is a one-story on slab commercial building of approximately 10,240 sq ft. It is a single-use building and is 100 percent occupied by a school. There have been no reported losses or damage to the building. The exterior walls are of frame construction with brick veneer covering. There is an 8 ft x 24 ft unheated exterior foyer that also has a brick veneer surface. The roof is wood truss with wood decking and shingle covering. The roof shingles are the originals from 2005 but appear to be in good condition. Several years ago, there was a lightning strike on the property. After that the insured had two lightning rods installed, which are connected to earthed grounds for dispersion. Interior walls and ceilings are Sheetrock with paint. The floors are vinyl plank in the high traffic areas, such as hallways, with epoxy finished non-skid concrete in the classroom areas, with area rugs in some places. Utilities appear safely arranged and according to local code. Plumbing is a mixture of copper and PVC with the assumption that PEX or its equivalent is being used inside the slab, with copper going to the faucets and other plumbing fixtures. Electric is BX cable with circuit breaker protection. All interior breaker panels and the exterior transfer switching equipment for solar power and HVAC units are in well maintained condition. Heating and air conditioning is HVAC. There are multiple exterior HVAC units (~10) which are protected behind a locked chain link fence.. All electrical, plumbing, and HVAC service is provided by Biggs Heating, Air Conditioning, Plumbing & Electrical of Garner NC. There is a residential washer and dryer in the utility room area, where the gas fired hot water heater is also located. The laundry area has good housekeeping, correctly vented dryers, clean lint traps, and no standing water. The small kitchen has a large residential-style microwave, along with a single commercial-grade electric range, which has 4 flat electric burners and an oven. The appliances are used solely for heating or reheating food. There is no food preparation done on the premises, as all food is purchased premade. There is a fire suppression system above the electric range, and it shows a current cleaning and inspection date of March 2025. The previous owner of the property used a gas range with open gas burners. Town of Cary regulations required the exterior venting hood with a suppression system. The current owner replaced the gas range with an electric one but opted to keep the hood and suppression system in place, although he believes it may no longer be mandated by the town. There are both Type K and Type C extinguishers on the wall adjacent to the range, both with current inspection date tags. There is also a manual pull lever to activate the Ansul system. The contact states that there are a total of 16 fire extinguishers in the building, all of which have November 2024 tags. Extinguisher inspection and service are provided by Vigilant. Fire protection monitoring, alarming, and sprinkler service is provided by IDSS of Raleigh NC. Protection is provided by the Town of Cary, NC Fire Department - a career/paid organization that carries an ISO-Class 1 designation inside the town limits. Fire Station #6 is 3.93 miles from the insured structure. There is a small ornamental pond located 115 feet to the southeast, and a municipal fire hydrant 120 feet to the west. Sprinkler heads were visible, but access to the sprinkler room was not possible on this visit. The building has burglar alarms monitored by IDSS. Daytime business hour access to the manned reception desk is controlled by a numeric keypad with a lock and monitored by the staff person on duty. The sole activity at this location is to serve as a preschool for children in the surrounding area. The facility is licensed by the state to serve up to 186 children with current enrollment at 184. All exterior lawn areas are synthetic turf and resilient surfaces, and inside a secure locked chain link fence. Access to get photos of the rear of the building was not possible at this time due to locked gates.
